thread.title: Apple: A Media 'Bundle' Worth $37 Billion? - Barron's - iWorld

title: Apple: A Media 'Bundle' Worth $37 Billion? - Barron's - iWorld
text:
Photo: Bloomberg News By David Marino-Nachison Sept. 6, 2018 7:00 a.m. ET A $12.99 Apple (AAPL) monthly media “bundle” combining video, music and Texture magazines could lead to a business worth $37 billion in revenue by 2025, new research suggests.
In a Wednesday note, Morgan Stanley analyst Katy Huberty—who has an “attractive” rating and a $245 price target on Apple shares—examined the company’s efforts to build its media businesses by spending on video development, which it guesses might reach 50 million subscribers as a stand-alone, lower-price (say, $7.99) service by 2025. That would represent a business worth $4.4 billion in revenue.
Newsletter Sign-up But what about a “bundle” instead?
“Combined with Apple’s stand-alone streaming music business, which we project grows into an $18 billion revenue generator over the same time period (from roughly $4 billion at the end of [calendar] 2018, streaming video and music would become a $22 billion business by 2025, roughly equal to the size of Netflix (NFLX) and Spotify Technology (SPOT) combined today but just 8% of Apple’s 2018 projected revenue,” Huberty wrote.
But such a service might lack enough archival content to make it seem worthwhile, they wrote, making it less appealing and more hit-driven—and so Morgan Stanley suggested a bundle instead. Huberty’s argument:
More About Barron’s Next Learn more about Barron’s Next The Barron’s Next 50 ... it would allow for differentiation vs. established peers, 2) it would reduce dependency on big video hits early on, 3) it could be perceived as a “higher value” service by consumers, 4) users would only need to navigate one integrated payments platform for all of their video, music, and news services, and 5) it could drive greater user engagement, subsequently improving overall customer stickiness.
The $37 billion the company could generate would be 64% higher the Apple would generate with two stand-alone services, Morgan Stanley projects. They assume the company will ultimately offer both, leading to 2025 revenue between $22-$27 billion.
We first discussed the notion of “Apple Prime” way back in February , and covered another Morgan Stanley take on Apple services in March .
Apple shares are up 34% in 2018. All of the companies mentioned in this story are Barron’s Next 50 stocks.
